title: Bounded-error randomized space decision
statement: A finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ decides a Boolean language $L$ in space bounded by $s$ if it uses space at most $s$ and, for every Boolean string $x$, there is a time bound $T$ within which it halts. If $x\in L$, its probability of outputting true by time $T$ is at least $2/3$; if $x\notin L$, every choice sequence of length $T$ yields the output false.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols
$L$ is a language of Boolean strings
For every input string, some natural-number time bound exists
Accepted inputs have true-output probability at least $2/3$ by that bound
Rejected inputs yield false output for every choice sequence of length equal to that bound
